$comment: Rule catalog — framing. Standard 1. One requirement, covering the record that must exist before modelling begins. Not machine-checkable: whether a target definition is precise enough to label an observation unambiguously is a semantic question, and a check confirming a heading exists would be read as confirming the problem was well formulated.

rules.title: The problem is formulated in writing before modelling begins
rules.description: A record states what is being predicted, at what unit and for which population, what decision the output feeds, and the relative cost of each kind of error — and it exists before the first model is trained.
rules.rationale: Every later choice follows from these answers: the metric from the cost asymmetry, the split from the unit of prediction, the calibration requirement from the decision the output feeds. A project that skips the record does not avoid the decisions, it makes them implicitly and can never afterwards explain them.
rules.remediation: Write the formulation: target definition precise enough to label any observation, unit of prediction, deployment population, the decision consuming the output, and the relative cost of a false positive against a false negative. Qualitative cost is acceptable where quantitative is not available; silence is not, because it reads downstream as a claim of symmetry.
rules.evidenceExpected: A problem-definition document, or a model card whose intended-use and target sections carry that content, together with an attestation stating when it was written relative to the first model.
rules.$assuranceNote: Nothing automated establishes this. Presence of a document is visible; whether its target definition is unambiguous, whether the stated population matches the deployment population, and whether the record predates the modelling are all invisible to a repository scan.
